english.title: Enter a Greater Manchester Metrolink vehicle / station wearing clothing which was soiled / bearing obscene words etc
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) entered a Metrolink

(A)_[ vehicle]_
(B)_[ station, namely **(..SPECIFY STATION..),]_

whilst wearing clothing, **(..SPECIFY TYPE OF CLOTHING..), which

(C)_[was likely to soil the fabric of the seats of the vehicle]_
(D)_[bore obscene or abusive words or material, namely **(..SPECIFY WORDS/MATERIAL..), which may have caused nuisance or inconvenience to other passengers]_
english.legislation: Contrary to byelaw 11(l) and 2(2) of the Greater Manchester Metrolink System Byelaws, section 30 of the Greater Manchester (Light Rapid Transit System) Act 1988 and section 10 of the Greater Manchester (Light Rapid Transit System)(No.2) Act 1988

english.notes:
(i) Byelaw 2(3) provides that any person that is reasonably suspected of contravening or attempting to contravene this byelaw:-
(a) shall upon being requested to do so, give his name and address to any authorised officer;
(b) may be removed from any vehicle or from the system by force if necessary by any authorised officer.
(ii) Byelaw 2(4) provides that without prejudice to byelaws 2(2) and 2(3)the operator may, where a person has either been convicted of an offence on the system other than under these byelaws, or where a person has been convicted of any breach of these byelaws, by written notice to the person concerned prohibit that person from entering any vehicle or station and any breach of such a prohibition shall constitute a breach of these byelaws.
(iii) Byelaw 8(2) provides that nothing in these Byelaws nor in the Conditions of Carriage shall prohibit the bringing upon or the use upon the System of Guide Dogs.
